title: How do we change square centimetres to square inches?
description: One square inch is six point four five one six square centimetres, so every group of that size is one square inch. Dividing one hundred sixty one point two nine by six point four five one six counts the groups and gives twenty five square inches.
teaching_notes: One idea: to change square centimetres to square inches, divide by the area of one square inch, not by the length factor. Watch for students who divide by two point five four.

source: Convert 161.29 cm2 to in2, where every 6.4516 cm2 gives an in2
video_script.why: The child has changed one square inch to square centimetres and now goes the other way, from square centimetres to square inches.
video_script.substitution: The book question gives the area and the size of one square inch, so the numbers stay as in the book.
video_script.anchor: a sheet of area one hundred sixty one point two nine square centimetres, to be counted in groups of one square inch
video_script.payoff_line: One hundred sixty one point two nine square centimetres is twenty five square inches.

final_answer.spoken: one hundred sixty one point two nine square centimetres is twenty five square inches

maths_rules: 1 in2 = 6.4516 cm2, so every 6.4516 cm2 makes one square inch
check by rounding: 6.4516 is between 6 and 7; 160 / 7 is about 23 and 160 / 6 is about 27, so the answer lies between 23 and 27
video_script.design: One square inch is drawn as a square marked 6.4516 square centimetres. The whole area is a long strip, and the working counts how many such squares fit in it.
